properties.decision: apply_heal refuses a proposal whose tied merge carries no chosen_survivor starting with the release that carries #749. It does not first ship a release that still merges ties and only warns. The changelog's "What to do" line (ask the person which node to keep, set chosen_survivor, apply again; or take the operation out to keep both) is the notice, and Alex is told with that release.
properties.name: A merge nothing separates is refused from the next release on, with no deprecating release first; Alex hears with that release
properties.rationale:
THE OWNER'S WORD. Anthony, 2026-10-14, on PR #749: "Merge 749 and go with your recommendation". The recommendation he took was: keep the refusal as built, because it replaces quietly deleting the wrong node and takes away no tool or field; the alternative was one release where a tie still merges but warns, with the refusal in the release after.

WHY IT WAS ASKED. req:the-mcp-server-keeps-working-as-is-and-door-improvements-are-additive-or-opt-in, amended on his word 2026-10-13: anything a client can call or read retires through a deprecating release first. #749 removes no tool, argument, field or node type, and the surface test passed against v0.84.0's record. One accepted call does narrow: a client that passed propose_heal's proposal straight back to apply_heal was applied before, and is now refused when the proposal holds a merge nothing separates. The refusal writes nothing, and what it replaced was a deletion decided by the alphabet (fact:root-cause-a-merge-deletes-the-wrong-node-because-the-survivor-rule-is-blind-to-status-priority-and-connections-2026-10-14). He chose to ship the refusal at once rather than keep that deletion alive for a release.
